pub fn get( &mut self, key: &FileKey, path: Option<&str>, ) -> Result<&CacheValue, Miss>

The value cached for the file whose current key is key, if it is still valid, and marks it recently used. path is where the file was seen now (through a hard link, say); it is recorded as the entry’s latest path, and the byte bound is enforced again.

A hit or miss is counted in Self::metrics. A miss for a changed file drops the stale entry.

Source

pub fn peek(&self, key: &FileKey) -> Option<&CacheValue>

The value cached for key, without counting a lookup or changing recency: for comparing with a fresh hash when the cache is not trusted to skip one (HashVerifyMode::must_recompute).

Source

pub fn path_of(&self, key: &FileKey) -> Option<&str>

The latest path recorded for the file key identifies (whatever its change stamp), if it is cached.

Source

pub fn insert(&mut self, key: FileKey, path: Option<String>, value: CacheValue)

Caches value for the file whose current key is key, replacing any entry for the same file. Tiers of an older version are not stored; if no tier is left, the old entry is still dropped.

Source

pub fn key_of(&self, volume_serial: u64, file_id: [u8; 16]) -> Option<&FileKey>

The key cached for the file with this ID, if any: for the change journal consumer (#60), which knows a file only by its ID and needs the cached key (and so its USN) to decide what a journal record means for it.

Source

pub fn rekey_after_rename( &mut self, new: FileKey, new_path: Option<String>, ) -> bool

For the change journal consumer (#60): every journal record for the file after its cached USN, up to new’s, is a rename and nothing else, so its key is now new and its path new_path. The entry is carried over.

The consumer must have checked that: find the cached key with Self::key_of, and read the journal from its USN. Only a strong entry can be rekeyed, and only to a strong key for the same file (volume and file ID) with the same journal, last-write time and size, and a later USN. Anything else could let a stale entry describe changed content, so the file’s entry is dropped instead. Returns whether it was kept.

Source

pub fn evict_file(&mut self, volume_serial: u64, file_id: [u8; 16]) -> bool

Drops the entry for the file with this ID, if any: for the change journal consumer (#60), which evicts as soon as it sees a change. Returns whether one was dropped.

Source

pub fn evict_path(&mut self, path: &str) -> bool

Drops the weak-key entry for this path, if any. path must be the same normalised match key as in FileKey::Weak: the lookup is an exact string match.

Source

Drops every entry.

Source

pub fn export(&self) -> Vec<CacheRecord>

Every entry, least recently used first, as records to persist.

Source

pub fn import( &mut self, bytes: &[u8], mac_key: &MacKey, ) -> Result<(), RecordError>

Decodes a persisted record and caches it. A record that fails its MAC is not cached and is counted as a tamper event; one that is malformed is not cached either.
